doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: To foster the continued safety and quality of Boeing's products, the Aerospace Safety Committee is a permanent committee of the board. As we continue working to return the 737 MAX to service around the world, the Board is focused on listening to all our key stakeholders to ensure we continually identify and implement new opportunities to improve the safety of our airplanes.
finding: The chair presents the Aerospace Safety Committee as a permanent board committee and frames safety as a standing board agenda item, not a crisis measure.

doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: Following last year's Annual Meeting of Shareholders, the Board amended Boeing's corporate governance principles to acquire an Independent Chairman of the Board. I work closely with the other independent directors and our CEO to ensure effective Board oversight of the company's strategy, operations and culture, anchored by our shared values of safety, quality and integrity.
finding: Since 2020 the governance principles require an independent chair; the chair describes the board as overseeing strategy, operations and culture, anchored on safety, quality and integrity.

doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: Today, we also announced the Board's decision to extend the company's age 65 standard retirement to age 70 for Boeing's CEO, Dave Calhoun. ... Given the substantial progress Boeing has made under Dave's leadership as well as the continuity necessary to thrive in our long-cycle industry, the Board has determined that it is in the best interest of the company and its stakeholders to allow the Board and Dave the flexibility for him to continue in his role beyond the company's standard retirement age.
finding: The board justified waiving the CEO retirement age by the continuity a long-cycle industry needs: an explicit long-horizon argument from the board itself.

doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: Let me close my introductory remarks by emphasizing that we're committed to ensuring Boeing has a diverse and engaged Board with a balance of skills and tenure. With a focus on safety, diversity, engineering, aerospace and risk management experience over the last 2 years, we've added 4 new independent directors. The Board is committed to continuing this refreshment process, culture of transparency and accountability, including through regular dialogue with our shareholders.
finding: After the MAX crashes the board refreshed itself toward safety, engineering, aerospace and risk-management skills and committed to regular shareholder dialogue.

doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: Item 2, 87% of the votes were in favor of the advisory vote on executive compensation. ... Item 4, 36% of the votes were in favor of the proposal seeking an additional report on lobbying activities. And Item 5, 35% of the votes were in favor of the proposal on written consent. ... We will continue to use your feedback to inform our decision-making going forward.
finding: In 2021 shareholders backed the board's pay plan (87%) and voted down two shareholder proposals (36% and 35% support); the chair says shareholder feedback informs board decisions.

doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: As we think about long-term strategy as a Board, we're a long-cycle business and where that ends is that our shareholders and our stakeholders end up being aligned. ... So we view those 2 very much in sync and think they work together. And what's good for our stakeholders is good for our shareholders on a long-term basis.
finding: The board describes its strategy lens as long-cycle and long-term, with shareholder and stakeholder interests aligned over the long run.

doc: Shareholder/Analyst Call (2021 Annual Meeting of Shareholders)
speaker: Lawrence Kellner, Chairman of the Board
quote: For the remainder of the Board Ed Giambastiani, Dave and myself, have significant aerospace expertise. And Lynn Good, Ron Williams and Bob Bradway add valuable outside perspectives from nuclear, health care, pharmaceutical industries, which allows the board to have a broader view of safety, manufacturing and operating issues and risk.
finding: The board recruits directors from other safety-critical, regulated industries (nuclear, health care, pharma) to widen its view of safety and operating risk.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO (former independent lead director and chair)
quote: As you well know, over the last year, the entire Boeing Board has been actively engaged in helping to resolve our current challenges and enhancing our governance and safety oversight. These actions included establishing a Board Safety Committee and realigning and elevating safety management and engineering organizations across the company.
finding: The MAX crisis turned the full board into an active participant in safety oversight, including creating a board safety committee and reorganising engineering and safety management.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: What if I told you I simply had a front-row seat to everything you saw? And so all the things I read and see and hear, make no mistake, they all have an impact, they have an effect, and I get a front-row seat. And ultimately, our Board took action as a result of it. And now I'm the one sitting in the operating seat.
finding: The new CEO, previously the board's chair, presents the December 2019 CEO change as the board acting on what it saw; the board's stated reason (restoring confidence with regulators, customers and other stakeholders) is in BG-0048.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: And every one of these programs lasts for decades and decades, every one of them. And that's how I think about everything I do inside The Boeing Company. I think my Board understands it, and I trust that they will evaluate me on that basis whether or not compensation schemes are perfectly aligned.
finding: The CEO says the board evaluates him on decades-long programme outcomes even when the pay formula is shorter-term: the board's judgement overrides the formula.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: But Larry Kellner, who is our Chairman, if you don't mind standing up for a second. He weathered that storm, and he's done a remarkable job of reconfiguring the Board. I want to mention to you just a few because I don't want to miss it. We've had 7 new members of our Board, all value-added folks. Steve Mollenkopf was the first, and this is all sort of that post-MAX moment, an engineer's engineer, smart, he interfaces with all of our technical programs. Admiral John Richardson oversaw the naval fleet, all things nuclear in the submarine area, all things safety.
finding: By 2022 the board had added seven post-MAX directors; Mollenkopf (now chair) was the first, an engineer who works with the technical programmes, and Adm. Richardson brings naval nuclear safety experience.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: Lynne Doughtie, who joined us from KPMG and who sits on our Board and the Audit Committee and has been a value add. Akhil Johri, former UTC CFO, long aerospace history, a lot of experience, runs Our Audit Committee and does it incredibly well. David, who I view as the single best propulsion guy on the planet, the best. He joined us, and he leads our Safety Committee. ... General Stayce Harris, she's a pilot ... She knows the Boeing equipment, knows the airplane, knows the cockpit
finding: Committee leadership in 2022: Johri (ex-UTC CFO) ran Audit, Joyce (ex-GE Aviation CEO, propulsion) led the Safety Committee, Doughtie (ex-KPMG) sat on Audit; Gen. Stayce Harris brings a pilot's view of Boeing airplanes.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: And then most recently, David Gitlin, of course, runs a very ... successful company, Carrier, but has real deep roots in his time with Raytheon and UTC. He knows this industry. He knows it well. He's a member of the Safety Committee. And again, we did what we think the governance world asked us to do, which is to populate the Board with people who really know this industry and have depth and are willing to get their hands dirty.
finding: David Gitlin (Carrier CEO, ex-UTC and Raytheon) sat on the Safety Committee; the refreshed board is meant to be hands-on and industry-literate, a response to the pre-MAX criticism that it lacked aerospace depth.

speaker: Greg Hyslop, Chief Engineer
quote: The reviews are characterized by transparency. The FAA attends every week at the BCA safety review. And these reviews have enabled us to identify risks more quickly and get them elevated to Dave and to our Board of Directors. Dave mentioned we established our Aerospace Safety Committee of our Board.
finding: Safety risks from the weekly business-unit safety reviews are escalated to the CEO and the board; the Aerospace Safety Committee is the receiving end.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: So we took on a lot of debt. Shareholders told us it would be great if you got rid of that debt sooner rather than later. And so we've been focused on free cash flow. It is a great metric, period, in terms of how we measure all of our people and the work that we're doing.
finding: After the crisis, shareholders pushed for early deleveraging, and free cash flow became the metric by which management is measured.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: I want that sort of future duration to be as long as the Board wants it to be. I have no specific contract term or anything of the sort. They'll tell me what it is.
finding: The CEO serves at the board's pleasure with no contract term: the board, not the CEO, sets the tenure.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: First, you saw the news that the company has announced the appointment of Kelly Ortberg as my successor commencing August 8 of this calendar year. As you know, the Board conducted an extensive search process. It was led by Steve Mollenkopf. ... He's had more than 35 years of experience in aerospace and is tremendously respected in the industry.
finding: The board chair ran the 2024 CEO search that chose Kelly Ortberg, an outside aerospace operator with more than 35 years in the industry.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: The Board made this decision. Over the last 9 months, when I think about the number of people they've called around the industry, the supply side, the buy side, the regulatory side, pretty remarkable, thorough discussions. ... So I wasn't really in the decision-making process, so I don't want to kid you about that.
finding: The board ran the CEO choice independently of the outgoing CEO, after consulting suppliers, customers, investors and regulators.

speaker: David Calhoun, President and CEO
quote: First of all, the process we have in place is a good one. Steve Mollenkopf in the Chair role, Bob Bradway in the governance role. The Board at large, they're going to look at the market every way they can.
finding: Board roles in 2024: Mollenkopf chair, Bradway leading governance; the whole board runs succession.

speaker: Brian West, CFO
quote: So this is the Board's question, the Board's call. ... They have solicited feedback from customers, from investors, from other stakeholders.
finding: Management defers CEO selection entirely to the board; the board consults customers and investors.

speaker: Dennis Muilenburg, Chairman, President and CEO
quote: The process we're talking about here, the decision process is identical to what we've used in all of our previous programs. So this year's decision is what we call authority to offer. That's based on a business case and our ability to go and have deep, detailed discussions with customers.
finding: New airplanes pass a two-gate process: authority to offer (on a business case) and then authority to launch (on launch-customer response); B-1479 and B-1586 give the second gate.

speaker: Greg Smith, CFO
quote: That's intentional, absolutely intentional and holding ourselves accountable to that original business case. And don't take your eye off that commitment we made to ourselves, to our board and to our shareholder.
finding: Investments are approved on a business case that management commits to the board and is then held to.

speaker: Julie Johnsson (Bloomberg) and W. James McNerney, Chairman and CEO
quote: And has the board approved you staying on past age 65? ... Yes, the heart will still be beating. ... Yes, I'll -- there's no end in sight.
finding: Asked whether the board had approved him staying past 65, McNerney answered yes (half in jest) and said there was no end in sight: the board let the CEO stay past the standard retirement age in 2014, as it did for Calhoun in 2021 (BG-0003), a pattern of favouring CEO continuity. The approval is implied by the CEO's answer; no board statement is in the record.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: Our Board of Directors has overall responsibility for risk oversight, with its committees assisting the Board in performing this function based on their respective areas of expertise. Our Board of Directors has delegated oversight of risks related to cybersecurity to two Board committees, the Audit Committee and the Aerospace Safety Committee, and each committee reports on its activities and findings to the full Board after each meeting.
finding: Risk oversight is a full-board responsibility; committees work by area of expertise and report to the full board after each meeting, so decisions are taken by the full board on committee findings.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: The Aerospace Safety Committee provides oversight of the risks from cybersecurity threats related to our aerospace products and services. The Aerospace Safety Committee receives regular updates and reports from senior management, including the Chief Engineer, the Chief Aerospace Safety Officer, and the Chief Product Security Engineer
finding: The Aerospace Safety Committee hears directly from the Chief Engineer and the Chief Aerospace Safety Officer, so engineering and safety readiness reach the board without passing only through the CEO.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: The award payout can range from 0 % to 200 % of the initial PRSU grant based on cumulative free cash flow achievement over a three-year period from January 1 of the grant year as compared to the target set at the start of the performance period. The PRSUs granted in 2024 also include a product safety downward modifier pursuant to which the payout following the end of the three-year performance period may be reduced by 25 % or down to 0 % if two specified product safety operational goals are not timely completed.
finding: The long-term incentive the board sets pays on three-year cumulative free cash flow, with a product-safety modifier that can cut the payout to zero: a medium horizon with safety as a gate.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: Performance-Based Restricted Stock Units (PBRSUs) are stock units that pay out based on the Company's total shareholder return (TSR) as compared to a group of peer companies over a three-year period. The award payout can range from 0 % to 200 % of the initial PBRSU grant. During 2023, these performance awards expired with a payout of 0 %.
finding: The earlier relative-TSR awards paid nothing in 2023; the board has since moved long-term pay from share-price returns to cash generation and safety.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: On October 30, 2024, we issued 129,375,000 shares of common stock, $ 5.00 par value per share, from shares held in Treasury Stock. As a result of the transaction, we received cash proceeds of $ 18,181 , net of underwriting fees and other issuance costs. ... On October 31, 2024, we issued 115,000,000 depositary shares, representing 5,750,000 shares of our 6.00 % Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock ... As a result of the transaction, we received cash proceeds of $ 5,651 , net of underwriting fees and other issuance costs.
finding: In October 2024 the company raised about $23.8B net of fees ($18.2B of common stock plus $5.7B of mandatory convertible preferred): dilution accepted to protect the balance sheet (the purpose, keeping the investment-grade rating, is in BG-0062).

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: We currently maintain investment grade credit ratings; however, Moody's downgraded our short term and long term credit ratings to Baa3/P-3 in April 2024. Moody's and S&P placed our ratings on review for downgrade in September 2024 and October 2024, respectively. In January 2025, Moody's affirmed the Baa3/P-3 investment grade credit rating with negative outlook.
finding: The rating sits one notch above junk at Moody's (Baa3, negative outlook in January 2025): any spend that threatens it is the board's first financial red line.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: the portion of Boeing's Corporate Governance Principles and Director Independence Standards, each as in effect on October 28, 2024, that requires Boeing to have at least 75% independent directors
finding: The governance principles require at least 75% independent directors.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: Mortimer J. Buckley – Director Steven M. Mollenkopf – Chair of the Board
finding: Steven Mollenkopf signs as Chair of the Board in February 2025.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: The Charter authorizes the Board, without any further approval, to (1) divide the preferred stock into series, (2) designate each such series, (3) fix and determine dividend rights
finding: Equity issuance terms (preferred series, dividend rights) are the board's to set without a shareholder vote: capital raises are a board decision.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: We also expect to require up to $345 million of cash per year for the payment of dividends on the outstanding shares of our 6.00% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (Mandatory convertible preferred stock), through the mandatory conversion date of October 15, 2027. Dividends accumulate at a rate per annum equal to 6.00% on the liquidation preference thereof, which is $1,000.00 per share, payable when, as and if declared by our Board of Directors. ... If dividends have not been declared and paid for six or more dividend periods, whether or not for consecutive dividend periods, the holders of such shares of Mandatory convertible preferred stock, will be entitled at our next annual or special meeting of shareholders to vote for the election of two additional members of our Board of Directors
finding: Dividends are declared by the board; skipping six preferred dividends would hand preferred holders two board seats, so the board must keep about $345M a year of preferred dividends funded until October 2027.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: During the first quarter of 2020, our Board of Directors terminated its prior authorization to repurchase shares of the Company's outstanding common stock and suspended the declaration and/or payment of dividends until further notice.
finding: In the 2020 crisis the board ended the buyback authorization and suspended the dividend to protect liquidity.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: On December 17, 2018, the Board approved a repurchase plan for up to $ 20,000 of common stock. In March 2020, the Board of Directors terminated its prior authorization to repurchase shares under this plan.
finding: The board's last buyback authorization ($20B, December 2018) came three months before the MAX grounding; buybacks are a board-authorized programme.

speaker: The Boeing Company (10-K)
quote: Cash dividends have been paid on common stock every year since 1942.
finding: As of the FY2018 10-K the board had paid a dividend every year since 1942 (77 years to 2018), and it kept paying until the March 2020 suspension (BG-0034); the 2020 suspension broke a long tradition and shows how far the crisis shifted priorities.
